en: Mayon Volcano in Albay is famous for its perfectly symmetrical cone shape visible from many surrounding towns.
During the dry season, the grass covering the Chocolate Hills in Bohol turns brown, resembling chocolate mounds.
Tubbataha Reefs Natural Park in the Sulu Sea contains vibrant coral reefs visible just below the ocean surface.
Visitors can observe massive limestone stalactites and stalagmites hanging from the ceiling inside the Puerto Princesa Subterranean River.
The Philippine tarsier, found in Bohol, has enormous eyes that are larger than its brain to see at night.
The Banaue Rice Terraces in Ifugao feature stepped paddies carved directly into the steep mountain slopes.
From the Tagaytay ridge, observers can clearly see the main crater lake situated within Taal Volcano.
During summer months, observers can spot massive whale sharks filtering plankton in the coastal waters of Donsol, Sorsogon.
At night, thousands of synchronous fireflies light up the mangrove trees along the Oyster River in Bohol.
Every evening, observers can watch giant sea turtles crawling onto the sandy beaches of Turtle Islands, Tawi-Tawi to lay eggs.
Visible steam rises from the natural hot springs in Tiwi, Albay, heated by underlying geothermal volcanic activity.
Massive, sheer limestone cliffs towering over clear turquoise waters are a prominent observable feature of El Nido, Palawan.
